raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. My father farmed it, and his father before him. I know this soil. The ground here is flat, the water table is reachable, and wheat-corn is what we grow here — everyone grows wheat and corn. I have about 8 mu of land. Half I'll put into winter wheat, half into summer corn after harvest. That's the rotation. That's what makes sense.

For wheat, I'll plant the same improved variety the seed shop has been selling — reliable, the village chief used it last year and did well. I'll apply fertilizer generously at base and top-dress at jointing. Water costs money but you can't skimp — I'll irrigate at seeding, jointing, and heading at minimum, maybe again at grain fill if it's dry. Spray once for aphids in spring, once for powdery mildew. Rotary till before seeding like always.

For corn, I'll go with hybrid seed — Xianyu 335 or whatever's available at the supply shop. No-till directly into the wheat stubble to save time and fuel. Summer rains usually handle most of the water, but I'll irrigate once during silking if it looks dry. One spray for corn borer, one for late blight if needed. Fertilizer base plus topdress at 10-leaf stage.

I'm not trying anything new this year. New things can fail and I can't afford a bad year.
